A_general.open_code_note: No official repository or package was found in links.json or the prepared repository folder. The hosted service is described by Polar, but its implementation is not public.
other_official_servers: Polar documents one remote MCP endpoint, https://api.polaranalytics.com/mcp, for MCP-compatible clients. Claude and ChatGPT also have documented app integrations to this service; no separate product endpoint or tool set was found.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Polar says an existing Polar customer is required to query a workspace. Pricing is quote/demo-led and plan-based; the pricing page includes Polar Headless MCP under AI Agents but publishes no numeric MCP price. The ChatGPT app article specifies a Polar Personal or Team plan. No separate per-call MCP charge was found.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Polar pricing is presented as Core and Custom plans; the page’s prices are not rendered as amounts in the captured evidence and directs users to book a demo. The software agreement describes monthly or annual subscription terms and a seven-day free trial.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Official pricing terms describe GMV-based bracketed recurring pricing, with an alternative contracted total GMV commitment/flat-price contract; product-specific pricing is confirmed in the Order Form. MCP access is included as part of a paid Polar product offering; no MCP call quota or per-call price was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires a Polar workspace and bearer credential/token pair. ChatGPT setup requires a Personal or Team plan and ChatGPT Apps availability, which may depend on the ChatGPT plan and region. No MCP-specific rate or call quota was found.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor controls subscription and service access; workspace administrators control connected sources, workspace definitions and roles. The documented service token is generated within Polar.

It does not publish MCP tool annotations or a complete parameter schema for the list.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Official API-use documentation describes report output with data rows, totals and a Polar deep link; get_context returns conversation_id, workspace, metrics and dimensions. Other tool result/error structures are not published in the sources reviewed.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 in the supplied pre-fetched evidence. The supplied public metadata at both protected-resource URLs and the authorization-server URL identifies issuer https://ai-service.polaranalytics.com; authorization, token and dynamic registration endpoints are published. Grant types are authorization_code and client_credentials; PKCE method is S256. No scopes_supported, token auth methods, expiry or revocation fields are present in the supplied JSON. Polar’s setup documentation instead describes a bearer token pair generated in app.polaranalytics.com/mcp, formatted as TENANT_ID|SERVICE_TOKEN. The metadata endpoints returned HTTP 200 in the supplied evidence; OIDC configuration returned 404.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The endpoint’s unauthenticated request received HTTP 401. No authenticated response was obtained.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official list includes read tools and writes to Polar (custom metrics, dimensions, labels, memory), plus file/Slack actions. Polar says connected source systems are not modified. No MCP annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation is documented. Polar advises users to read back a proposed definition change before approval. 3. The endpoint requires authorization. Supplied OAuth metadata lists authorization_code and client_credentials and PKCE S256, but no scopes_supported or token lifetime/revocation. Docs describe a tenant ID and service token. Role inheritance and admin toggles are not documented. 4. No read-only mode, tool filter, URL mode, sandbox endpoint or region-specific MCP endpoint found. 5. Polar describes governed workspace metrics and says only data required for the current question is sent to AI models; no MCP-specific PII masking or field-level scope details found. 6. No MCP rate limits, quotas, bulk caps or result truncation documented. Pricing page mentions 15-minute refresh for custom metrics/dimensions, not a call limit. Official API docs say totals are returned and should be used instead of recomputed sums. 7. Published API-use docs give required arguments for a subset of tools; validation, coercion and unknown-argument behavior are not documented. 8. General policy describes infrastructure logging/monitoring; MCP call audit details are unknown. 9. rate_report records report feedback; no published description establishes whether it prompts for feedback or sends a rating automatically. 10. No initialize instructions or server-delivered skills documented; a prompt library is published outside the MCP tool list. 11. update_memory is explicitly described as durable workspace knowledge for later conversations. Its exact effect on later outputs is not described. 12. The documented endpoint is a single hosted Polar endpoint over a semantic layer aggregating connected sources; no sub-server hierarchy is documented. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, or script execution tool appears in the 37-tool official list. Polar separately says SQL access is a product add-on, not an MCP-listed tool.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Always use the totals returned by the API instead of recomputing sums from rows.

Treat it the way you would treat edit access to a shared dashboard. Read the plan back before approving anything that changes a definition, and keep write access to the people and agents that need it.
get_connector_statuses and get_data_integrity_report exist for exactly that reason: check them before you trust a number that looks surprising.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One documented hosted endpoint presents the Polar tool set over its semantic layer. Its aggregation of many upstream data connectors is the product’s data model, not evidence of dynamically loaded MCP toolsets or nested MCP servers.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool list at https://www.polaranalytics.com/mcp-for-ecommerce/polar-analytics names 37 tools and gives no separate total by category. All 37 names are included in actions.json. No catalogue-only tools were added. The Claude connector directory lists 11 of these names; MCP.so had no tool list available; VerifyMCP reported 33 available components but stated that it could not capture schemas because authentication was required; SourceMedium did not provide an authenticated official endpoint schema. The official list therefore governs the count. Parameter schemas are published only for a small subset in Polar’s API-use article.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Polar recommends using returned totals instead of recomputing sums, checking connector status and data integrity before trusting surprising numbers, and reviewing a plan before approving definition changes. The reviewed docs do not establish these as server-enforced restrictions.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Polar describes the semantic layer as applying workspace metric definitions consistently and says: “No writes to your sources: nothing is sent back to your store, your ad accounts or your ESP.” The product page also says the MCP only sends to AI models “the data required to answer your current question, nothing more.” The policy/DPA describes tenant isolation, security logging, return/deletion on request or termination subject to legal retention, and optional AI features with data not used for model training and abuse-detection retention of about 30 days.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Polar says answers use governed, reconciled metrics, include totals, and can link back to reports. It advertises 45+ connectors and a semantic layer with workspace-specific definitions. The legal terms describe SaaS availability subject to planned maintenance and external outages.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The 37-tool official list includes writes to Polar definitions and workspace memory, while the source-system no-write promise is consistent with Polar’s stated boundary. No public implementation exists to verify enforcement. Totals and suggested checks are documented behavior/guidance, but no server-side enforcement mechanism is described. Data-minimization, training and retention statements are policy/product claims; MCP-specific handling is not separately detailed in the public tool documentation.

contradictions: The submitted documentation URL, https://intercom.help/polar-app/en/articles/12960325-using-mcp-tools-as-an-api, returned HTTP 404 in the prepared evidence. The accessible official support article is https://support.polaranalytics.com/articles/8432442750-using-mcp-tools-as-an-api; it documents the same API-use topic.

VerifyMCP reports that it could not retrieve/validate protected-resource metadata during its 27 October 2026 scan, while the supplied pre-fetched responses for both protected-resource metadata paths returned HTTP 200 with OAuth metadata. The supplied endpoint evidence is used here.

Polar’s MCP page documents the tenant/service-token bearer format, while the supplied OAuth metadata advertises authorization_code and client_credentials grants, PKCE S256 and dynamic registration. The sources do not explain how these authorization approaches relate.
observations_for_research: The official tool list combines analytical reads with writes to Polar’s own semantic definitions, labels and durable workspace memory; the vendor separately draws a boundary against writes to connected commerce and advertising systems.

The semantic-layer design supplies business-defined metrics and returned totals, potentially constraining the agent’s interpretation and arithmetic; the documentation advises using totals but does not describe enforcement.
The durable update_memory tool is described as affecting later conversations, indicating a persistent state surface distinct from ordinary report retrieval.
notes: Inspected links.json, links_check.txt, the prepared official pages and scripts, endpoint captures, and the code folder/commit inventory. No official public code, package, registry-linked source repository, MCP schema capture or initialize instructions were found. The official page provided the only complete tool-name list. It does not publish parameter schemas for most tools or MCP annotations; actions.json marks those parameters NOT PUBLISHED. The separate Intercom URL supplied as input returned 404; the matching Polar support article was available on support.polaranalytics.com. Unofficial/community catalogue content was not used as evidence for official tool definitions.
